subject: FoxPoint renewal — escrowed credits & interop staging plan
messages:
From: Alyssa Kline <alyssa.k@foxpoint.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@foxpoint.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — credits and packaging options

Jonas,

Hope you had a good weekend. Our renewal for the pilot environment is coming up in September and procurement asked me to gather a clear set of commercial options so they can compare vendor replacement economics. Two quick asks from our side:

- Can you outline how "escrowed credits" would work operationally (vesting schedule, usable scopes, and whether they can be applied to Dedicated capacity)?
- We also want to see a simple comparison: upfront prepay vs tiered credits vs pay-as-you-go with a migration assistance package (high level $ impact for our current usage).

I attached our Q2 usage so you can map numbers to an example. Procurement will need SOC 2 evidence and a Docusign-ready contract if we get to terms. Timing: procurement wants a commercial sketch by 8/20 to present to leadership.

Thanks — appreciate a concise table + recommended option.

Best,
Alyssa
Alyssa Kline
Director, Cloud Architecture
FoxPoint

Attachments: current_usage_report_Q2.csv

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Kline <alyssa.k@foxpoint.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — credits and packaging options

Alyssa — thanks for the data and the clear ask. We can do that. High level (short summary for procurement):

1) Escrowed credits (recommended for low-risk retainers)
   - Credits placed in an escrow account and released on a quarterly vesting schedule (3, 6, 9 months).
   - Usable across Hosted API and Dedicated pools; cannot be used for 3rd-party infra costs (e.g., cloud egress).
   - If FoxPoint replaces us within 12 months, a pro-rata portion of unvested credits refunds back to Redwood; final off-ramp penalty negotiated.

2) Upfront prepay
   - Biggest immediate discount (up to ~20% on token rates) but non-refundable. Good if you want predictable unit economics.

3) Pay-as-you-go + migration assistance
   - Keep baseline PAYG, receive a one-time migration credit bucket (applied to onboarding + early egress costs).

For your Q2 numbers, I mapped three scenarios in a short counter (attached):
- Option A: 12-month escrowed-credit package — 30% credit pool, quarterly vesting; estimated 11% unit-cost reduction.
- Option B: 12-month prepay — full prepay at 18% discount; lowest unit cost but no escrow protections.
- Option C: PAYG + migration bucket — 8% equivalent uplift (credit offset) + 30 hours of onboarding support.

Next steps I suggest: I can send a single-page commercial sketch that shows: projected spend, net effective rate, migration support, and contract bullets (escrow mechanics, off-ramp). Can your procurement folks accept an escrow construct (escrow agent + release schedule) or do they prefer a credit-hold within Redwood with contractual vesting?

I attached a draft commercial sketch for your review. If that looks close, we can prepare a DocuSign-ready term sheet and SOC2 summary.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales — East
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_counter_offer_fp.docx

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: FoxPoint negotiation posture and counter framework

Team — quick internal note before we finalize the sketch to Alyssa. Key negotiation levers:

- Escrowed credits: we can offer up to 30% of projected 12-month ARR as escrow, with quarterly vesting (3/6/9/12). Recommend tying partial vesting to usage thresholds (protects Redwood from artificial churn).
- Prepay vs escrow: prioritize escrow as headline (reduces churn risk, gives procurement the "safety" they ask for). Prepay is our premium option.
- Migration assistance: offer 40 hours of engineering support + a $35k one-time onboarding credit for the first 90 days.
- Off-ramp: 60-day notice + pro-rata refund of unvested credits minus a 10% administrative fee.

Ask: Jonas — do we want to cap escrowed pool per-region? FoxPoint will likely want global credits; recommend we allow multi-region but exclude third-party infra egress as Jon suggested.

I'll finalize the single-page sketch and drop in the redlines for the term sheet. Attaching draft doc for comments.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_counter_offer_fp.docx

From: Alyssa Kline <alyssa.k@foxpoint.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@foxpoint.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 08:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — credits and packaging options

Jonas — appreciate the fast turnaround and the options. Procurement reviewed and came back with a preferred path and a few edits to the mechanics:  

- Preferred: Escrowed credits (structure you proposed) but credits must be held by a neutral escrow agent (not Redwood). Vesting schedule we can accept but want vesting at 3/6/12 (skip 9-month) and a maximum carry-forward of 3 months of unused credits.
- Escrow granularity: Credits must be fixed USD-denominated units (so they are not impacted by token-rate swings).
- Off-ramp: Procurement insists on a clearer penalty schedule; propose pro-rata refund of unvested credits minus a 5% admin fee, and require Redwood to cover documented egress costs up to $25k if we switch within 6 months.
- SOC2: attaching SOC2_summary.pdf. Procurement also wants confirmation of retention period and whether audit logs will be delivered on export.

We attached the SOC2 summary and a procurement checklist. If you can confirm acceptance of neutral escrow + the $25k egress coverage, we can route a simple term sheet to DocuSign and aim to sign by 8/25.

Thanks — Alyssa

Attachments: SOC2_summary.pdf

Alyssa — thanks, and thanks for the SOC2 summary. We can accept the neutral escrow requirement and the $25k capped egress coverage with one small edit: the admin fee on pro-rata refunds will be 7.5% (instead of 5%) to cover escrow agent costs; we can reduce that to 5% if FoxPoint agrees to a 14-month minimum term instead of 12.

Confirming the agreed points:
- Escrow: neutral escrow agent, USD-denominated credits, vesting at 3/6/12 months, 3-month carry-forward cap.
- Egress coverage: Redwood to reimburse documented egress up to $25k if off-ramp occurs within 6 months.
- Off-ramp admin fee: 7.5% (negotiable to 5% for 14-month term).
- Deliverables: Draft term sheet (DocuSign-ready), SOC2 export guidance, and the single-page economic comparison.

Next steps: Lauren will upload the final term sheet to HubSpot and attach the DocuSign link. I propose a short 30-minute sign-off call next Tuesday 8/25 at 10am PT to close the loop — does that work for you?
